div.head: Quadr II Praef 14.1
div.ab: Quem Deus felicibus auspiciis et salutari, quesumus, corporis et anime prosperitate, cum inclita coniuge sua Mathilde secunda et eorum liberis, longis seculorum seculis et eterna pace gentis nostre faciat imperare!
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 543 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: May God, we pray, make him rule with happy auspices and salutary prosperity of body and soul, with his renowned wife Matilda the second and their children, for long ages of ages and in the eternal peace of our people!

note.seg: 22 quavis wie S. 5474 liest Stubbs, ‘every’ übersetzend. Die älteste Hs. von Hn aber, nämlich Rs, schreibt aus quesumus
22 Stubbs reads quavis, as on p. 5474, translating ‘every’. But the oldest MS. of Hn, namely Rs, writes out quesumus in full
